title: "cvode() and the CVODES adjoint"

`cvode()` compiles a model against SUNDIALS CVODE/CVODES ($\ge 6.0$) of the build host for the
`solveODE()` interface of `cppODE()`. [Notation](methods-overview.html#notation); arguments
`method`, `derivMode`, `asaCheckpoints` of [`cvode()`](../reference/cvode.html), `gradtol` of
[`adjointControl()`](../reference/adjointControl.html).

## Comparison with `cppODE()` {#comparison}

|                       | `cppODE()`                                        | `cvode()`                       |
|:----------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------|
| `method`              | `bdf`, `adams`, `rb4`, `tsit5`                    | `bdf`, `adams`                  |
| `derivMode`           | `forward`, `reverse`, `forward-reverse`; `deriv2 = TRUE` | `forward`, `reverse`     |
| forward sensitivities | dual numbers                                      | sensitivity equations, JVPs     |
| reverse mode          | discrete adjoint of the computed steps            | continuous adjoint (CVODES ASA) |
| second order          | forward over forward, forward over reverse        | none                            |
| reverse options       | `keepStore`, `store`, `adjointControl()`          | `asaCheckpoints`, `adjointControl(gradtol = )` |
| libraries             | LAPACK; KLU optional                              | SUNDIALS $\ge 6.0$; KLU optional |

Table: The two ODE backends, with the same model arguments and `solveODE()`. JVP:
Jacobian-vector product.

## Shared code and arguments

Shared with `cppODE()`:

- the code generator; $J = \partial f / \partial x$ formed on the
  [expression graph](methods-codegen.html#codegen) and emitted with linear tables and loops;
- the arguments `events`, `forcings`, `rootfunc`, `fixed`, the returned object, and the column
  order, shapes (state-only, full, partial) and row names of `tangent` and `parms`;
- the chain rule $S_\theta = S_p\,\partial p / \partial \theta$ of
  [Forward (2)](methods-forward.html#eq-sensitivity-theta);
- the linear solver: KLU for $n_x \ge 8$ and structural density of $J$ at most $0.4$ if
  SuiteSparse was found at install, dense LAPACK otherwise; `sparse = TRUE` requires KLU;
- PCHIP forcings, discontinuous event resets, root events at zero crossings of a user function.

## Differences between the backends

**Sensitivity right-hand side.** CVODES integrates
[]{#eq-cvodes-sens}
$$
  \dot S_k = J(x, p)\, S_k + \frac{\partial f}{\partial p_k},
  \qquad k = 1, \dots, n_p, \tag{1}
$$
as one generated Jacobian-vector product of $f$ per direction $(S_k, \partial p/\partial\theta_k)$,
in `double`, without $J$ and without tangent storage. `cppODE()` evaluates $f$ on dual-typed
state, [Forward (1)](methods-forward.html#eq-sensitivity-p), for all directions in one pass.

**Methods.** CVODE has only the multistep families
([stability](methods-stepping.html#stiffness-and-the-choice-of-method)) and first-order
sensitivities (no `deriv2 = TRUE`).

**Events.** Generated glue outside CVODES applies the first-order Heun transport
[Events (2)](methods-events.html#eq-fixed-heun) with the firing time
[Events (4)](methods-events.html#eq-dt-star-first); CVODES re-initializes the sensitivities from
it.

## Adjoint sensitivity analysis {#asa}

`cvode(..., derivMode = "reverse")` compiles the CVODES adjoint sensitivity analysis (ASA) instead
of forward sensitivities and returns the `$cotangent`
[Reverse (1)](methods-reverse.html#eq-adjoint-contraction) of a native reverse solve, states
first; the rest of the call, batch entry point included, is unchanged.

**Backward problem.** CVODES integrates [Reverse (2)](methods-reverse.html#eq-adjoint-ode) as a
separate ODE [@cao2003adjoint], right-hand sides emitted as vector-Jacobian products of $f$
([code generation](methods-codegen.html#codegen)) without $J$:
[]{#eq-asa-system}
$$
  \dot\lambda = -\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}\!\lambda,
  \qquad
  \dot q = -\left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial p}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}\!\lambda, \tag{2}
$$
the second the quadrature [Reverse (5)](methods-reverse.html#eq-adjoint-quadrature) with
$q(T) = 0$. Both run from $T$ to $t_0$, the minus signs cancelling against the reversed limits, so $\lambda(t_0)$ and $q(t_0)$ are the state and parameter
parts of the gradient. By default $q$ is outside the error test: gradient entries of very
different scale would stall the backward step against `reltol` alone. `adjointControl(gradtol = g)`
adds it with absolute tolerance $g$, so the step size controls the gradient error, as the
[checked sweep](methods-reverse-checks.html#refine) of the native mode does for discrete steps.
The backward problem is a BDF solve at the tolerances and step budget of the call, with the
forward linear solver (KLU for a sparse model) and the analytic Jacobian $-J^{\mathsf T}$, formed
from $J$ in the forward pattern.

**Checkpoints.** CVODES stores a checkpoint every `asaCheckpoints` accepted steps (default $200$,
trading memory against re-integration) and recovers $x(t)$ between checkpoints by re-integrating
from the earlier one and interpolating. With interpolated states, the gradient is the derivative
of no discretization performed, within
$O(\mathrm{tol})$ of both the exact gradient and the derivative of the reported value.

**Jumps at observations.** $\lambda$ starts from the last cotangent row; at each earlier
observation the sweep adds that row, the jump condition of
[Reverse (2)](methods-reverse.html#eq-adjoint-ode). The problem restarts only at nonzero rows;
at every output time it would reduce the method to first order at unobserved times.

**Several cotangents.** Cotangent columns share the checkpoints but need one backward integration
each, where the native mode sweeps the stored checkpoints once per column. `keepStore`,
`store` and the other `adjointControl()` options have no counterpart: CVODES manages checkpoints
and backward step size, and a continuous adjoint has no discrete steps with errors to estimate,
weight or report.

**Events.** CVODES cannot be re-initialized within a recorded forward run, so a model with events
is integrated in stretches between jumps (a single one without events), each stretch with a CVODES memory,
checkpoints, root functions and linear solver, starting from the post-jump state. The sweep runs
them last to first, each from the adjoint of the later one, with the jump transpose in between:
for $x^+ = R(x^-, p, t^{*})$, $\lambda^- = (\partial_x R)^{\mathsf T}\lambda^+$ and the gradient
gains $(\partial_p R)^{\mathsf T}\lambda^+$, plus the terms of a firing time that moves with $p$
or, for a root $g_e(x, t, p) = 0$, with the state,
$\delta t^{*} = -(\nabla_x g_e\,\delta x + \partial_p g_e\,\delta p)/\dot g_e$, as in
[the adjoint of an event](methods-reverse-events.html#event-adjoint) of the native mode. Root
finding is off on a stretch before the sweep, since a root found again while CVODES recomputes the
forward solution between checkpoints would label the stored data with that root time.

**Restrictions.** A reverse model has no forward sensitivities, and `cvode()` has no second order; Hessians, or
gradients consistent with the returned value, need the native backend.
